title: Promote-and-Observe: automated eval handoff, retrospective hooks, and rollback playbook for catalog & tenant pins
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: When catalog models are promoted (catalog-wide upgrades) or customers perform tenant-level model pins/upgrades, we need a standardized 'promote-and-observe' workflow that not only triggers automated eval suites but also hands off results to stakeholders, attaches a short retrospective hook, and enables an automated rollback path if regressions exceed thresholds. Goal: implement a promotion orchestration flow that (1) runs targeted smoke + canary evals, (2) surfaces deterministic pass/fail signals to tenant dashboards and runbooks, (3) creates an automated retrospective ticket skeleton and attachments (PR links, eval diffs, example failures), and (4) wires automatic rollback triggers with human-in-the-loop confirmations for high-impact failures.
acceptance_criteria: A promotion (catalog or tenant pin) invokes a configurable eval pipeline that runs a small prioritized testset within 0-15 minutes of the event
Eval results are attached as artifact links to the promotion event and to a generated retrospective ticket template
Promote dashboard shows pass/fail and delta vs golden baseline with token-level latency and quality breakdowns

If predefined regression thresholds are hit (e.g., >5% quality drop on high-priority testset OR severe latency increase >50ms p95), a rollback can be auto-initiated or queued for human approval depending on impact tier
Runbook links, relevant PRs, and a short summary are auto-populated in the retrospective ticket to accelerate triage
Engineering owners are paged only for high-impact failures; medium/low issues create watch-only notifications and a scheduled post-mortem task
engineering_notes: Trigger mechanics: subscribe promotion events from catalog + tenant pin APIs; push event into eval-orchestrator queue with priority tag (catalog: high, tenant: medium) — ENG to add event schema extension for 'promotion_context'
Eval selection: use prioritized per-model testset S1 (golden examples) + a lightweight sampling S2 based on live traffic distribution; limit run budget to ~250 synthetic requests for smoke
Threshold config: allow per-project overrides; default thresholds defined in policy table (QA_drop_pct=5, latency_p95_increase_ms=50)
Cost tradeoff: keep default suites small to control cost; provide optional 'deep-check' for enterprise customers (on-demand heavier runs billed separately)
Rollback behavior: two modes — auto-rollback (catalog promotions only for low-risk models), and gated-rollback (requires human approval for tenant-pinned upgrades marked as 'sensitive')
Observability: emit structured events for eval-run.start, eval-run.complete, eval-diff.summary to metrics & event logs; integrate with console rollouts page
Privacy/compliance: eval pipelines must honor tenant data isolation — synthetic test queries only, no replay of customer data without explicit consent
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (alpha): wire basic event trigger + smoke eval for internal catalog promotions only; surface results in internal CI channel
Phase 1 (beta): enable tenant-pin events for opt-in customers; create retrospective-ticket template and dashboard widget
Phase 2 (general): default-on for catalog promotions; provide tenant-level opt-in toggle and per-tenant threshold overrides
Phase 3 (safety automation): enable auto-rollback for low-risk model types and human-in-the-loop approvals for sensitive upgrades; add paging policies
